newsitem.title: INDIA: REPORT INDIA'S CHIDAMBARAM TO RESIGN "SPECULATIVE".
newsitem.headline: REPORT INDIA'S CHIDAMBARAM TO RESIGN "SPECULATIVE".

text.p: A spokeswoman for Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram on Thursday called a newspaper report that said he was considering resigning "highly speculative".
The Business Standard said Chidambaram was considering the possibility of resigning after the government was forced on Thursday to withdraw the insurance regulatory bill from parliament.
"Yesterday he (Chidambaram) categorically said 'no' when asked if he would resign," the spokeswoman said.

After the bill was withdrawn from the lower house of parliament on Wednesday, Chidambaram was asked by a reporter if he would like to "shoot down" speculation that he would resign following the withdrawal of the insurance bill.
"What is there to shoot down? Resignation is the easy way out," he said. "A reformer has to be patient."

The Business Standard said Chidambaram told officials and close advisers that he felt severely let down after the government failed to muster enough votes to defeat an opposition-backed amendment to bar foreign firms from the insurance sector.
It said he would discuss the matter with the leader of his Tamil Maanila Congress party, G.K. Moopanar.
The Hindu newspaper said in a front-page story that Chidambaram had ruled out resigning.
